metadata.title: HD 271791: An Extreme Supernova Runaway B Star Escaping from the Galaxy

evidence.quote: HD 271791: AN EXTREME SUPERNOVA RUN-AWAY B STAR ESCAPING FROM THE GALAXY

A measurement of the proper motion of the bright
(V = 12.26 mag) early B-type giant HD 271791 allowed the
Galactic rest-frame velocity to be determined to lie within the
range 530 – 920 km s<sup>−1</sup>, exceeding the local Galactic escape
velocity and thus qualifying the star as a HVS – and the place
of birth to be constrained to the outer rim of the Galactic disk
at a Galactocentric distance of{ \gtrsim } 1 5kpc (Paper I).

HD 271791 is escaping from the Galaxy, it could be termed
a hyper-runaway star, the first of its class.

values.condition: Galactic rest-frame speed range determined from the proper-motion measurement (Paper I) and restated in the conclusions.

notes: HD 271791: previously identified as an HVS in Paper I and followed up here; the final assessment retains it as escaping the Galaxy (T:p1-b10, T:p4-b31). No additional identifier is provided in the supplied text.

HD 271791: No present-day equatorial coordinates, parallax, distance, proper-motion components, or radial velocity are numerically reported. The Galactocentric distance of ≳15 kpc in T:p1-b10 refers to the star's place of birth, not its present-day three-dimensional Galactocentric radius, so it was not recorded. The 630 km/s value is a separate Galactic-rest-frame speed for the “best” proper motion, not a replacement for the 530–920 km/s range.
